alex: Quick heads-up — I ran a cross-benchmark today comparing our synthetic queue-emulator harness vs recorded-replay for continuous batching. Putting raw notes here.

alex: High-level numbers: synthetic peak tps ~4800, mean latency ~28ms, p95 ~120ms. Replay peak tps ~4200, mean ~32ms, p95 ~85ms. Replay has lower tail which is surprising.

mira: Do we have KV cache warmup diffs? Replay preserves session prefixes so kv-hit could be higher.

alex: Yep — replay kv-hit ~63% after warmup, synthetic ~18% (no warmup). I scraped /metrics kv_hit_ratio. Also noticed kernel selection diverged: synthetic mostly chose float16-cuda-opt, replay ended up on int8-llm-kernel for longer sequences.

kevin: What were batch_cap and max_delay for the runs? The harness defaults can hide behavior.

alex: I swept batchcap 32/64/128 and max_delay 10/30/50ms. Synthetic used batchcap=128 max_delay=50ms by default. Tail flips with max_delay — at 10ms tail drops a lot but throughput drops ~20%.

ben: Any perf reg flags?

perf-bot: perf-bot: regression detected on 1919002468 — tail latency increased 12% vs baseline (2026-03-01) for workload 'chat-short'. Alert created, investigate kernel scheduling.

tara: Can you paste the minimal repro command? I'll try a kernel swap locally.

alex: ```
./bench --mode replay --trace path/to/trace.tar \
  --batch-cap 64 --max-delay-ms 30 --kernel-policy auto \
  --kv-prefetch on --seed 42
```

alex: I also forced kernel-policy=prefer-int8: on replay mean latency dropped ~6%, but synthetic got worse — quant path misbehaved for short sequences because of frequent kernel switches.

kevin: Hypothesis: synthetic generator yields higher microburst variance -> more kernel switches -> hurts queueing fairness and tail. Replay's temporal locality helps kv cache and stabilizes kernel selection.

ben: Can we simulate a warmed KV in synthetic? e.g. run a prefix population pass then steady-state.

alex: Tried that: 5k prefix warmup in synthetic bumped kv-hit to ~55% and tail approached replay within ~8%.

mira: How about tenant fairness? Synthetic single-tenant is optimistic. Did you try multi-tenant interleaving?

alex: Yes — 3-tenant interleave (A: short, B: medium, C: long). With batchcap=128 and max_delay=50ms tenant A was effectively starved: median latency 30ms vs baseline 12ms. Lowering batchcap to 32 improved fairness but throughput dropped.

tara: Maybe tune dynamic batch cap per-tenant based on ETT. Can we try delaycap driven by ETT?

kevin: We have an ETT prototype. Suggest we run: same trace, swap scheduling policy (global batchcap vs ETT-driven) to be apples-to-apples.

alex: Agreed. Next steps: 1) run synthetic with warmup + deterministic seed, 2) rerun kernel-policy experiments (int8 vs float16), 3) run ETT scheduling vs global batchcap on same multi-tenant trace, 4) capture pprof + nvprof to collect kernel churn samples.

ben: :thumbsup: I'll own the ETT runs. Tara take kernel swap. Mira add KV metrics + dashboards.

mira: I'll add kv_hit_ratio, kernel_switch_count, batch_size_hist to the per-route dashboard and pin to this thread.

alex: Quick tail log example:
[2026-03-12T14:22:10Z] rpc recv reqid=abcd ms=3 batch=45 kernel=int8 switch=true kv_hit=false
[2026-03-12T14:22:11Z] rpc recv reqid=efgh ms=2 batch=2 kernel=float16 switch=false kv_hit=true

perf-bot: perf-bot: added alert link: https://redwood/perf/alerts/1919002468

tara: I'll try local repro with env var REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=prefer-int8 and post results.

kevin: We should also normalize sequence length histogram to ensure apples-to-apples. Synthetic sampled 'short' generator; replay had a mix. I'll produce a blended synthetic generator that matches replay's seq-len histogram.

alex: Thanks team — kicking off 48h runs now and will post summarized CSVs + raw traces. Ping me if you want the raw traces before the summary.
